text:
Braeden Bowman went undrafted, came up through the Henderson Silver Knights and is now in his second season as a Golden Knights depth forward. Seven points in 21 games at under 13 minutes a night is about what the role asks, and his game-tying snipe against Detroit, a little drag to change the angle before beating Daniil Tarasov's glove, was one of the better goals of Vegas's road trip.

The numbers around him have been unkind. Vegas has scored seven fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back. His own finishing is fair (four goals on 4.6 expected). Less encouraging, the team takes 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him out there, more than six points worse than without him, on a club that normally controls play.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting his share of passes across the slot last season, but rarely carrying the puck in himself. His minutes have slipped over the last ten games. On a deep team, that's the number to watch.
